items.front: Write the three core deficit formulas.
items.back: Fiscal Deficit = Total Exp − (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital Receipts) = total borrowing. Revenue Deficit = Rev Exp − Rev Receipts. Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments.
items.examPoint: Types of deficits — fiscal, revenue, primary, effective revenue & monetised (formulas)

items.back: Revenue Deficit − Grants for creation of capital assets. Isolates the truly non-asset-creating revenue gap.
items.examPoint: Types of deficits — fiscal, revenue, primary, effective revenue & monetised (formulas)

items.front: Are borrowings and disinvestment revenue or capital receipts?
items.back: Capital receipts — they create a liability (borrowings) or reduce assets (disinvestment/loan recovery). Interest RECEIVED is a revenue receipt. Tax + non-tax with no liability = revenue receipts.
items.examPoint: Revenue budget vs capital budget — receipts & expenditure classification

items.front: FRBM Act 2003 — key targets & who reviewed it?
items.back: Centre fiscal deficit ≤3% GDP; general-govt debt ≤60% GDP (Centre 40%, States 20%). Escape clause (Sec 4(2)) for calamity/security. NK Singh Committee (2016) → debt-to-GDP anchor.
items.examPoint: FRBM Act 2003 — targets, escape clause & NK Singh Committee

items.front: Three government funds and their control.
items.back: Consolidated Fund (all revenue/loans — needs Parliament's nod, except charged expenditure); Public Account (PF/small savings — govt as banker); Contingency Fund (President, unforeseen needs).
items.examPoint: Government funds — Consolidated Fund, Public Account & Contingency Fund

items.front: Most inflationary way to finance a deficit?
items.back: Creation of new money (monetising the deficit / borrowing from RBI). Deficit financing in India is used mainly for economic development.
items.examPoint: Instruments of fiscal policy & fiscal consolidation; deficit financing methods

items.front: GST — amendment, date, what stays OUTSIDE it?
items.back: 101st Constitutional Amendment (2016), live 1 July 2017; destination-based dual tax (CGST+SGST intra-state, IGST inter-state). Outside GST: petroleum, diesel, petrol, gas, ATF, alcohol, electricity.
items.examPoint: GST — 101st Amendment, dual GST (CGST/SGST/IGST) & destination-based principle

items.front: GST Council — article, chair, voting weights, majority.
items.back: Article 279A; chaired by Union FM; Centre 1/3 + States 2/3 of votes; decisions need 3/4 majority; quorum 1/2.
items.examPoint: GST Council — Article 279A, composition & voting (Centre 1/3, States 2/3, 3/4 majority)

items.back: Effective 22 Sep 2025: two primary rates 5% & 18% + a 40% sin/luxury rate (0% for essentials); the 12% and 28% slabs were removed. '5-18-40'.
items.examPoint: GST 2.0 (2025 rate rationalisation) — two-rate 5%/18% + 40% sin/luxury, effective 22 Sep 2025

items.back: Article 280 (President, ~every 5 yrs). 14th FC (Y.V. Reddy) raised States' share 32%→42%; 15th FC 41%; 16th FC = Arvind Panagariya, award period 2026-31 (constituted 31 Dec 2023).
items.examPoint: 16th Finance Commission — Panagariya, 2026-31 award period; 15th FC 41% devolution

items.front: Direct vs indirect tax boards; which taxes were abolished?
items.back: Direct (progressive, unshiftable) → CBDT; Indirect (regressive, shiftable) → CBIC. Abolished: Wealth Tax (2016), Dividend Distribution Tax (2020). VAT = destination-based STATE subject.
items.examPoint: Tax classification — direct vs indirect; CBDT & CBIC

items.front: BEPS and tax buoyancy — what do they mean?
items.back: BEPS (Base Erosion & Profit Shifting) = OECD initiative curbing MNC tax avoidance. Tax buoyancy = %Δ tax revenue ÷ %Δ GDP (includes rate changes); elasticity excludes discretionary changes.
items.examPoint: Tax concepts — buoyancy, elasticity, tax-to-GDP, Laffer curve, Pigovian & Tobin taxes

items.front: AP 2026-27 — GSDP and the two headline deficits.
items.back: GSDP ~₹19.75 lakh cr; fiscal deficit 3.8% of GSDP (₹75,868 cr); revenue deficit 1.1% (₹22,003 cr). AP FRBM Act 2005; State FC under Arts 243-I/243-Y.
items.examPoint: AP deficits & debt 2026-27 — fiscal 3.8%, revenue 1.1% of GSDP; outstanding debt ~35% of GSDP
